cells.tense: This is finishing now, and you are standing in it able to say plainly what it cost you.
cells.ask: Before the week ends, tell one person what this cost you and what it was for. Not to be thanked — so it has a witness.
cells.core:
You know what you spent to get here, and you don't hide it. That's rarer than it sounds. People tend to either bury the cost or turn it into a story about how much they suffered. You do neither. You say what you gave up and what it was for, and the people around you can feel that it's true.

What this balance needs next is a hand on the tap, not a wider opening. Care that keeps choosing its direction at the same pace is what holds here — not more pouring. Growth that doesn't exhaust itself, space held without clutching it. Go much further in the same direction and it stops being tending and starts being proving, and proving has no end. Hold what you've made at the size it already is, and let it keep growing on its own time.
cells.sheetLine: You can name what it cost, and make something with it.
cells.verb: naming what was given up so the giving is seen
cells.place: where direction gets chosen and attention is spent on purpose

cells.tense: You are already living in the moment this gets seen, and spending today's attention on making it arrive.
cells.ask: Pick one thing in front of you and get it exactly right — the wording, the number, the fit — and leave the rest until tomorrow.
cells.core:
You're spending credit you haven't been given yet. Somewhere ahead is the day the sacrifice gets seen, the day it finally counts, and you're making decisions from inside that day instead of this one. It comes out as pushing — one more push, one more proof, and then they'll get it.

The thing slipping is your aim. When everything is worth proving, nothing is; effort spreads thin across causes that don't need it. Steady your hand before you spend one more day on this. Pick the piece that actually matters this week and bring that one thing to a fine edge, precisely, without asking anyone to notice. Choice, not pressure — the difference is whether the work gets sharper or just louder.

cells.tense: The effort still moves out of you, and you stand where aiming it used to come easily.
cells.ask: Put one long thing on the calendar for yourself this week and keep the appointment — the boring hour, the same chair, no audience.
cells.core:
Effort is still moving out of you. What stopped is the part where it gets aimed. Decisions that used to come easily now sit open — and while they sit, the same load gets carried day after day with no finish line anyone can see.

What's low isn't your strength. It's the aiming — and that's the part you can practice, plainly, without waiting to feel like it. So don't try to feel more about any of it; add one structure instead. An unbroken hour on the one thing no one asked you to carry. It'll feel small and it still counts. Sticking with something ordinary, in a form you can repeat next week, is what puts the current back in the line. A finish you can actually reach is one week of standing in the same place.

cells.tense: You are the one directing this already, and you describe it as if it were happening to you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you do for someone and have been calling necessity, then say out loud it's your choice.
cells.core:
You pick the direction around here more than you let on — what gets prioritized, who gets covered, what gets let go. You do it well and quietly, and when it comes up you describe yourself as just managing what's in front of you. The steering is happening. The ownership isn't said.

That's why it can feel like there's no time, no room, no say. When your own choices go unnamed, they come back as obligations. You don't need a bigger effort here; you need a smaller, truer description. One thing you keep doing on purpose, admitted as yours. Once it's named, it stops running you, and you can decide whether it's still worth keeping or whether it's time to put it down.

Reader objection: 'I'm not waiting to be thanked, I just want to get on with it' — which is compatible with Balanced and with Too Little, so the read may miss. The ask survives being wrong: honoring someone else, tending, honing, and naming what gets kept are all useful acts regardless. Sentence that serves the writer: none about a stage or a parade — every line about witnessed sacrifice has to resolve into something the person can do today.
